name: ikunix Packivio – Packing Station & Order Fulfillment for WooCommerce
author: ikunix

sections.description:
ikunix Packivio adds a mobile packing station to WooCommerce with order packing, packing time tracking and employee accountability.

A permanently free packing station with a private address and worker PIN, digital order details, packing notes, start/stop/complete timers, basic history and statistics.
WooCommerce HPOS is supported. Successful packing can set Ready for shipment automatically. The optional Order prepared email is controlled separately in WooCommerce email settings.

Every feature included in this plugin is available without purchasing a licence. There is no trial expiry, paid upgrade switch, activation-code form or paid feature code in this package.
The Plans & pricing tab includes a comparison and links to the separately available Premium add-on for Pro and Business. Paid licence activation takes place only in that add-on.

External service and privacy

The plugin uses the ikunix Packivio service at https://fulfillment-api.ikunix.at for installation registration, authoritative timer start/end timestamps and timing results.
The first connection is initiated by selecting Connect Free. New packing sessions require internet access and the connected service.

The service receives installation identifiers, the shop identifier, pseudonymous order/worker references, item counts and technical timing/request information. IKUNIX uses existing service records to produce aggregate service-usage statistics; a download alone is not tracked as an active installation.
Customer names, addresses, email addresses, detailed order contents, packing notes and any previously stored packing photos remain in your WooCommerce store. No separate analytics or advertising service is added.

Service terms: https://ikunix.at/agb
Privacy policy: https://ikunix.at/datenschutz
Service information and support: https://ikunix.at/plugins/packivio/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install and activate ikunix Packivio.
  3. Open WooCommerce > ikunix Packivio > Plans & pricing and select Connect Free.
  4. In Settings, configure your packing profiles and PINs, visible order statuses and language.
  5. Open the private packing-station address and start packing.

The service connection is free and does not require an IKUNIX customer account.
Back up your store before updating. Versions before 0.14.0 use a different plugin directory: first deactivate the old Premium add-on (if installed), then the old base plugin. Do not uninstall either plugin. Install and activate the new ikunix-packivio package, then install and activate ikunix-packivio-premium 0.14.0 or newer if needed. The new packages reuse the existing shop identifiers, worker profiles, settings and history; no new activation code is needed for a previously bound licence. Later updates under the new slug replace the installed version normally.
Keep the old packages inactive. To remove their files after the successful switch, delete only their old plugin directories using your host’s file manager. Do not use WordPress’s Delete action for the old base: its historical uninstall routine may erase shared data if cleanup was enabled.
The interface supports English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Czech, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Finnish, Hungarian, Romanian and Turkish.
Bundled translations support the independently selected plugin language. WordPress language-pack translations take priority when they match that language; missing strings use the bundled translations.
sections.faq:
Is Free a trial?

No. Free remains usable without a subscription and has no trial expiry.

Do I need an activation code?

No. Select Connect Free to connect the free timing service.

What happens to existing data after an update?

Existing shop identifiers, worker profiles, PINs and saved data are retained. All plans support unlimited worker profiles, including after a downgrade.

What happens when the service is unavailable?

New timers cannot start until the connection is restored. Existing local order history remains available.

Which packing details can I see in a WooCommerce order?

Free shows a compact Packing details box with completed/stopped attempts, packing duration, completion date and packing notes. The separate detailed timeline and packing-photo view are part of the Premium add-on for Pro and Business. Previously recorded proof remains readable with that add-on if a subscription ends.

Can I delete the packing history of one order in Free?

Yes. In Settings > Data & reset, enable per-order fulfillment history deletion and save. Open the WooCommerce order and use the trash button in Packing details, then confirm. WooCommerce managers can delete that order’s local packing history; an active packing session must be stopped first. The order, its status, items and WooCommerce order notes are retained. Its packing sessions are removed from local ikunix Packivio statistics. Any previously linked packing photos stay in the Media Library but are detached from ikunix Packivio. This does not erase the external service’s timing records.
To pack the order again, also set it to a status included in your packing-station queue and refresh the station.
sections.changelog:
0.14.2

  • Load settings scripts through WordPress while preserving the existing settings layout.
  • Make packing-station messages available to WordPress translation tools and prefer matching community translations.
  • Protect translation-file entry points while retaining all supported interface languages.

0.14.1

  • Correct the Premium add-on version in the migration instructions and clarify the service name.
  • Keep the packing workflow and existing data unchanged.

0.14.0

  • Rename the plugin to ikunix Packivio with the ikunix-packivio directory and text domain.
  • Include unlimited workers and full profile management in Free, Pro and Business.
  • Preserve existing data and previous packing-station links when migrating.

0.13.0

  • Previously introduced the PackFlow directory and text domain ikunix-packflow.
  • Prevent loading the old and new plugin runtimes together and document the data-preserving directory transition.
  • Retain shop identity, licences, worker PINs, station links, settings and packing history.

0.12.4

  • Keep the WordPress compatibility declaration in this readme, as required by Plugin Check.
  • Complete translations for Free setup, service notices and shared session errors in all supported interface languages.
  • Verify compatibility with WooCommerce 11.2.2; existing installations, licences and packing history are retained.

0.12.3

  • Complete the relevant email-control translations in all 16 interface languages.
  • Verify the email and per-order history deletion messages in the effective translation catalogue.

0.12.2

  • Refresh the email overview status and preview format immediately after saving WooCommerce email settings.
  • Keep saved email preferences and package permissions separate.

0.12.1

  • Add the optional per-order history trash button and cleanup result to Free’s Packing details box.
  • Keep active sessions protected and retain the separate detailed timeline in the Premium add-on.
  • Clarify order-history access and deletion in the documentation.

0.12.0

  • Introduce the previous PackFlow name while retaining existing installation identities and saved data.
  • Correct the settings reset destination and register station assets through WordPress.
  • Improve output escaping, database cleanup and translation catalogue isolation.

0.11.2

  • Restore the production settings layout with separate cards and save actions.
  • Restore Plans & pricing with Connect Free, monthly/yearly comparisons and IKUNIX links.
  • Keep paid licence activation exclusively in the separate Premium add-on.

0.11.1

  • Keep the Settings and Service connection content below the navigation tabs.

0.11.0

  • Dedicated permanently free packing workflow and service-connection screen.
  • Retain existing installation data when updating.
